text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of free mediastinal air on the chest X-ray, combined with your history of forceful retching and subsequent chest pain, strongly suggests a perforation of the esophagus. This is a medical emergency known as Boerhaave syndrome, and we need to initiate immediate surgical consultation and broad-spectrum antibiotics.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Esophageal Rupture (Boerhaave Syndrome)
